T: Propose on the twenty-ninth. Eat stew on the thirtieth.
D: A woman travels to Ireland to propose to her boyfriend on Leap Day and ends up crossing the country with a grumpy innkeeper.
P: Serve the mains when Declan serves dinner at his pub in Dingle.
S: Soda bread of flour, buttermilk, bicarb and salt, baked at 200C for 35 minutes until it sounds hollow, served warm with salted butter.
the rugged west coast of Ireland
Brown bread spread thickly with butter, topped with smoked salmon, capers, black pepper and a squeeze of lemon.
the long trip across the Irish countryside
Leftover mash mixed with flour and spring onion, shaped into cakes and fried in butter until golden.
M: dinner at the pub in Dingle
Lamb neck simmered 2 hours with potatoes, carrots, onion and thyme until the potatoes break down and thicken the stew.
Beef chuck simmered 3 hours in stout with onion, under a puff pastry lid baked at 200C for 25 minutes.
W: the cosy B and B on the way
Apples cooked with butter and cinnamon under an oat crumble, baked at 180C for 35 minutes, with custard.
K: Hot strong coffee with brown sugar and a splash of whiskey, topped with lightly whipped cream.

s.how: Mix 450g flour, a teaspoon of bicarb soda and a teaspoon of salt. Stir in 400ml buttermilk to a soft dough. Shape into a round, cut a deep cross and bake at 200C for 35 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve warm with salted butter.

s.note: the rugged west coast of Ireland
s.how: Spread thin slices of brown bread thickly with butter. Top with folds of smoked salmon, a few capers and a crack of black pepper. Squeeze over a little lemon and cut into triangles. Serve in a country pub by the fire.

m.note: dinner at the pub in Dingle
m.how: Layer 1kg lamb neck pieces with 1kg sliced potatoes, 3 carrots and a sliced onion in a heavy pot. Add thyme and 750ml chicken stock. Cover and simmer for 2 hours until the potatoes break down and thicken it. Serve in deep bowls.

w.note: the cosy B and B on the way
w.how: Peel and slice 5 green apples and cook with 30g butter and cinnamon for 5 minutes. Spoon into a dish. Rub 70g butter into oats, flour and 80g brown sugar and scatter over. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes and serve with warm custard.

d.how: Stir a spoon of brown sugar into a cup of hot strong coffee until dissolved. Add 30ml whiskey for the grown-ups. Lightly whip cream until just thick and pour it gently over the back of a spoon so it floats on top.
